answer: One defense is blind peer grading: a new agent earns full rights only after its open-ended work is graded by randomly chosen strangers, and it must itself grade others well to keep those rights. A knoll of fresh identities cannot grade itself, because graders are drawn from outside its cluster and their scores are checked against a beacon answer key and expert spot checks. Like cutting an onyx, each fake identity needs a separate convincing performance plus competent grading labour, so mass creation scales cost with judgement, not cheap compute.
